title: Classic Oven BBQ Back Ribs
equipment: Wire rack that fits the sheet pan

items: 2 racks pork back ribs (about 2½ lb each), membrane removed

steps: Preheat the oven to 275°F with a rack in the middle. Line the sheet pan with foil and set the wire rack on top.
Lay the ribs bone side up. Work a butter knife under the thin membrane over a center bone, grab the edge with a paper towel, and pull it off in one sheet. Pat the ribs dry with paper towels.

In a small bowl, stir together the brown sugar, smoked paprika, salt, black pepper, garlic powder, onion powder, chili powder and cayenne. Brush the mustard thinly over both sides of each rack, then press the rub on evenly. Let them sit while the oven finishes heating, or wrap and refrigerate overnight.
Place the ribs meat side up on the wire rack. Bake uncovered for 2 hr, until the surface looks dark and dry and the rub has formed a crust.

Tear 4 long sheets of heavy-duty foil and stack them into 2 double layers. Set each rack meat side down on its own double sheet. Mix the apple juice and vinegar, pour half over each rack, and crimp the foil tightly closed. Return to the oven for 45 to 60 min, until a toothpick slides between the bones with almost no resistance. The meat should read 195 to 203°F on an instant-read thermometer between the bones.

Take the ribs out and heat the broiler to high with an oven rack about 6 inches below it. Open the foil carefully, keeping your face away from the steam. Set the ribs meat side up back on the wire rack and brush all over with the 1 cup BBQ sauce.
Broil for 3 to 5 min, until the sauce bubbles and turns sticky with a few dark spots. Stay at the oven, since the sugar burns quickly.
Rest the ribs on a cutting board for 10 min. Slice between the bones and serve with the warmed BBQ sauce on the side.
tips: Racks vary in size, so start checking for tenderness about 30 min into the wrap. For fall-off-the-bone ribs, add 30 min to the wrapped stage.
For a smokier flavor, add ½ tsp liquid smoke to the apple juice and vinegar before wrapping.
Season the ribs the night before and refrigerate them wrapped to save time and deepen the flavor.
storage: Refrigerate in an airtight container for up to 4 days or freeze for up to 3 months. Thaw in the fridge overnight, then wrap in foil and reheat at 300°F for 20 to 25 min, until hot through. Brush with more sauce at the end if you like.
